findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys evaluate to "[object Object]"; all non-access_token fields are stripped
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are JavaScript computed property keys; calling `.toString()` on a Zod schema object yields the literal string "[object Object]", not a wildcard. Both keys collide (the second wins), so the schema is effectively `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() })`. Because `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, when credential sync is enabled every expiry/scope/instance_url field is dropped from the parsed result and no numeric expiry is ever validated. Downstream, Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)` = NaN, Office365 never gets an updated `expires_in`, and Salesforce loses `instance_url`/`id`/`signature` from the stored key. Use `.passthrough()` / `z.record` or an explicit refinement instead of computed keys.

findings.title: Google credential key is now persisted as the zod SafeParse wrapper `{success, data}`
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result object (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed data. The Google service writes this directly with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so after the first token refresh the stored `credential.key` becomes `{"success":true,"data":{access_token,...}}`. On the next instantiation `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails because `access_token`/`refresh_token` are no longer top-level, permanently breaking the Google Calendar integration for that user in both sync and non-sync modes. The code must store `parsed.data` (and the same wrapper is spread by Office365 and Salesforce via `.data`, so those happen to be fine).

findings.title: Injects the literal string "refresh_token" as refresh_token, overwriting real refresh tokens in callers
findings.body: When the refreshed response lacks `refresh_token`, the helper mutates `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Callers then copy this into the stored credential: Zoom does `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` (line 120 of zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts) and Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` over `o365AuthCredentials` (line 264 of office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, where `refresh_token` is `.optional()`). In either case the user's genuine refresh token is replaced with the placeholder string, and the next refresh against the real provider fails with invalid_grant, forcing the user to reconnect the app. The placeholder should never be written back; callers should preserve the existing refresh token when none is returned.

findings.title: Sync path returns a raw fetch Response but callers expect provider-specific shapes
findings.body: When `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `fetch` `Response` regardless of what `refreshFunction` would have returned. Several callers do not handle a `Response`: Google reads `res?.data.access_token` (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94-95) → TypeError; HubSpot treats the result as a `HubspotToken` and reads `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` and stores the Response object as `key` (hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192-198); Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error` expecting an axios response (zohocrm:217, zoho-bigin:96) → TypeError. So enabling credential sync breaks token refresh for Google, HubSpot, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin. Additionally `response.ok` is never checked, so a 4xx/5xx body is parsed as a token.

findings.title: Outbound request to the credential sync endpoint carries no authentication
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no secret/header. The endpoint returns live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs, so a self-hoster following this contract must expose an unauthenticated token oracle (or invent out-of-band auth). The inbound webhook uses `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`; the outbound call should send the same shared secret so the self-hoster can verify requests.

findings.title: Credential id passed where userId is expected
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes the credential's primary key as the third argument, but the helper treats it as the Cal.com `userId` and posts it as `calcomUserId` to the sync endpoint. The self-hoster will look up the wrong user (or none), and team credentials (userId null) are not excluded. Should pass `credential.userId`.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
findings.body: The new block calls `prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This fails type-check and at runtime throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` inside `getClient`, so every Salesforce service instantiation rejects and all Salesforce bookings fail.

findings.title: Salesforce now refreshes on every instantiation yet still uses the stale access token
findings.body: `getClient` unconditionally POSTs to `login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` each time the service is constructed (no expiry check), which adds latency and will hit Salesforce refresh rate limits. The newly obtained token is written to the DB but the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url` from the old key, so the refresh has no effect on the actual client. Also `response.statusText !== "OK"` is unreliable (HTTP/2 responses have an empty reason phrase) and will throw a 400 even on success; use `response.ok`. Finally, unlike other apps this call bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens`, so with sync enabled it still contacts Salesforce directly while `parseRefreshTokenResponse` applies the (broken) minimum schema.

findings.title: Webhook accepts any HTTP method and returns 500 on malformed bodies
findings.body: The handler does not restrict to POST, and `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError that is not caught, so an invalid payload produces an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 with a useful message. Likewise `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on a wrong key or non-JSON payload. Wrap in `safeParse`/try-catch and reject non-POST requests with 405.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`
findings.body: The shared secret header is compared using plain string inequality, which is susceptible to timing side channels. Also, if the configured header appears multiple times `req.headers[...]` is a `string[]` and the comparison always fails. Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers and normalize the header to a single string.

findings.title: No tests for the new sync helpers or webhook despite cross-cutting changes to 11 integrations
findings.body: The PR introduces shared logic (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`, the `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint) that is now in the token-refresh path for Google, Office365, Zoom, Webex, HubSpot, Lark, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin, MS Teams and Salesforce, and the author notes no tests were added or run. Several of the defects above (computed-key schema, SafeParse wrapper being persisted, Response vs. object shape mismatches, missing prisma import) would be caught by even minimal unit tests of the helpers with sync enabled/disabled and a type-check run.
